# SSH-003: Root cannot log in over SSH

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

root is the one account name every attacker knows, and a root session has no sudo step to log or limit it. PermitRootLogin yes allows a root password; prohibit-password (the default) still allows root with a key, which is usually a leftover from provisioning.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -i '^permitrootlogin'
```

## How to fix it

Log in as a sudo user (a dedicated non root user for the PaaS too), then set PermitRootLogin no.

## What a fix can break

Tools that connect as root (a PaaS, backup jobs, provisioning) must move to a sudo user first.

Run `stackward explain SSH-003` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
